Chat vs Project vs Cowork

Two choices, not three tabs: which mode you work in (Chat or Cowork) and which container holds your context (a Project or a folder). Knowing which to reach for saves real time. Here's what each is, when to use it, and where each one bites.
For Staff - Intermediate
STAFF REFERENCE
Quick frame

There's one Home tab. Two separate pickers in the composer decide how a task runs: a mode and a container. They're independent - you set both.

  • Mode - Chat or Cowork (a toggle in the composer). Chat answers you. Cowork does things - works with files on your computer, runs code, runs jobs on a schedule. You pick the mode per task.
  • Container - Project or folder (a separate picker). A Project is a claude.ai workspace pre-loaded with School Tech context and shareable with the team. A folder is a location on your computer that a Cowork-mode session reads on demand.
  • Put them together: "a Project" = a shared, STA-loaded workspace you normally use in Chat mode. "a Cowork project" = Cowork mode pointed at a folder. Mode and container are separate choices, not one setting.
Two dials, not three tabs. Older guides called Chat, Project, and Cowork separate tabs. They aren't - there's one Home tab, and you set the mode (Chat/Cowork) and the container (Project/folder) in the composer for each task.

Plain chat

What it is: Chat mode with no Project loaded - a fresh conversation with no STA setup. It knows nothing about us unless you paste it in, and it starts blank every time you open a new one.

Reach for it when: you want a quick reword, a definition, a one-off rewrite, or a personal question that has nothing to do with STA data.

STA examples: "Reword this sentence to sound friendlier." "What does SAML mean in plain English?" "Draft a quick thank-you note."

Watch out: it forgets everything when you close it, and it has zero School Tech context.
Projects

What it is: a chat that's pre-loaded with School Tech instructions and reference files (a built-in knowledge base). It already knows our products, customers, processes, and tone, so you skip the explaining and just ask.

Where you find it: a Project is a claude.ai Project - you open it from the Home tab and it loads its context automatically. Every staff tool - AI Advisor, STA Support Chat, Salesforce Cohort - is a Project. You normally work in a Project in Chat mode. A Project is a container (what context is loaded), not a mode - so "a Project" and "Cowork" aren't opposites; you can even open a Project in Cowork mode if you have access.

Our live Projects: AI Advisor (all staff), STA Support Chat (support team), Salesforce Cohort (any Salesforce user, mostly our SF admins).

Reach for it when: you're doing real STA work - troubleshooting, customer drafts, Salesforce guidance - or anything a teammate should be able to use too, since Projects are shareable.

Good to know: a Project keeps its setup files loaded every time, but it still won't recall yesterday's conversation unless that info lives in the project.

UNVERIFIED and never tested: whether connectors like Gmail and Drive work only in a PRIVATE project, and whether sharing a project with the team switches connectors off. No source and no verification date exists for that behavior, and nobody has tested it. Do not rely on it as a safety boundary until someone does. The test takes about five minutes: share a test Project that has Gmail enabled, open it as a second user, and attempt a send. Several other pages describe shared staff tools as unable to send or reach live systems, and those descriptions rest on this one sentence.
Cowork

What it is: Cowork mode - flip the composer from Chat to Cowork and Claude can take real action: read and write files on your computer, run code, run jobs on a schedule, and split big tasks into sub-tasks. It's the "do things for me" mode, not just "answer me."

Where you find it: it's a toggle in the composer on the Home tab, not a separate place - you pick Chat or Cowork per task, then point the session at a folder (the container) so it has somewhere to work. Desktop-only for file work: Cowork mode itself runs on web and mobile (beta), but the local file and browser access is desktop-only. At STA, file-access Cowork projects run on the AI Admin PC with the folder mounted - you can't run one from web or mobile.

Who has it at STA: admins and power users only.

Worth it when: multi-file work, a recurring or scheduled output (like a weekly digest), or a long multi-step job that would overwhelm a single chat. For anything that's just one question, use a Project instead - Cowork uses more of our usage allowance.

Scheduled jobs do NOT need your computer awake: scheduled tasks run remotely and fire even with the desktop app closed. The exception is any step that touches local files or the local browser - those need the desktop app open on the machine that holds the folder. So a task that only reads a connector and posts to Slack runs unattended; a task that writes into a mounted workspace folder does not.

Data caution - important: Cowork can read and write real files on your computer, which is a much bigger blast radius than a chat. School Tech's rule stands regardless of the tooling: never run student records, HR or employee PII, or any restricted data through Cowork. The data rule from the Getting Started guide applies double here.

On auditability: Cowork activity is captured in the Compliance API, and Team/Enterprise owners can stream those events to a SIEM - so "there is no audit trail" is not accurate. Anthropic's published guidance is to avoid granting Cowork access to sensitive local files; it does not prohibit regulated work outright. Our restriction is School Tech's own call, and it holds on its own merits.
Which one do I use?
  • Just need an answer, a definition, or a quick rewrite? → Plain chat
  • Doing real STA work, or something a teammate should use too? → a Project
  • Need it to touch files on your computer, or run on a schedule? → Cowork (and you're an admin or power user)
Common gotchas
  • Plain chat forgets everything the moment you close it.
  • Shared Projects lose connector access (Gmail, Drive) - keep a project private if it needs them.
  • Scheduled Cowork tasks run remotely - they fire with the app closed. Only the steps that touch local files or the local browser need the desktop app open.
  • Cowork uses more usage than a Project - don't reach for it for one-off questions.
  • Cowork is never for student, HR, or restricted data - that's School Tech's rule, not a gap in the tool (activity is captured in the Compliance API).
  • Mode (Chat/Cowork) and container (Project/folder) are separate picks - a Project isn't a mode, and Cowork isn't a tab.
  • Cowork mode runs on web and mobile, but file and browser access is desktop-only - STA's file-access projects run on the AI Admin PC.
